explanation: Appert sealed food in glass bottles and boiled them, winning a French government prize, decades before Pasteur showed that microbes cause spoilage. Nobody yet knew why it worked.

claims.text: Nicolas Appert published his method of preserving food by sealing it in bottles and heating them in 1810.
Louis Pasteur patented his process of heating wine to prevent spoilage, later called pasteurization, in 1865.
Appert received a prize from the French government for his food-preserving method.
Pasteur's work showing that microbes cause spoilage came decades after Appert's method.
